chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A woman from the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so is my husband. I gave him my belly (for bearing his children) and supported him in his worldly and afterlife affairs, yet he did not find anything displeasing in me. I complain about him to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to you.' He (peace be upon him) asked: 'From what are you complaining?' She said to him: 'He said to me today, "You are prohibited to me like the back of my mother," and he has thrown me out of my house. So look into my matter.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has not yet revealed to me a Book by which I may judge between you and your husband, and I dislike that I become one of the pretenders.' So she began weeping and complaining of what was with her to Allah and to His Messenger, and she departed.

So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, heard her argument with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) regarding her husband, and what she complained to him. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed a Quranic verse because of that.

Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your contention; indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing. (As for) those of you who put away their wives by likening their backs to the backs of their mothers, they are not their mothers; their mothers are no others than those who gave them birth; and indeed, they utter a hateful word and a falsehood; and indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent for the woman, so she came to him. He said to her: 'Bring me your husband.' So she brought him. He said to him: 'Did you say to this wife of yours, "You are prohibited to me like the back of my mother"?' He said: 'I had said that to her.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has revealed a Quranic verse regarding you and your wife.' So he recited to him what Allah had revealed from His Words: "Allah has heard the words of her who pleads with you about her husband" up to His Words: "Indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving." He said: 'Cuddle your wife to yourself, for you have spoken an evil from the speech and a fallacy. Allah has pardoned you and forgiven you, so do not repeat.'

So the man departed, regretful of what he had said to his wife. And Allah disliked that for the believers afterwards, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And those who put away their wives by likening their backs to the backs of their mothers, then withdraw what they said." Meaning what the first man said to his wife: "You are prohibited to me like the back of my mother." He said: 'So whoever says it after Allah has pardoned and forgiven the first man, then upon him is freeing a captive before they touch each other.' Meaning copulating with her. 'That is what you are advised for; and Allah is Aware of what you do.'

'So whoever does not find [a captive], then fasting for two consecutive months before they touch each other. And whoever is not able, then feeding sixty needy ones.' So Allah made the punishment for the one who does Zahaar after this prohibition this, and said: 'That is in order that you may have faith in Allah and His Messenger; and these are Allah's Limits.' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made this the limit of Zahaar.

Humran said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And Zahaar does not occur in a vow, nor in harming, nor in anger. And Zahaar does not occur except upon purity without copulation, with the testimony of two Muslim witnesses.'

key_terms.تَحَاوُر: Tahawur: Mutual contention or argument, specifically referring to the woman's argument with the Prophet regarding her husband.
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: Shahidan: Two witnesses, required for the validity of Zahaar in this narration.
key_terms.طُهْر: Tahar: Purity, specifically referring to a state of ritual purity and absence of sexual intercourse when Zahaar is pronounced.
key_terms.ظِهَار: Zahaar: A form of divorce in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia where a husband likens his wife's back to his mother's back, prohibiting sexual intercourse but not ending the marriage.
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Kaffarah: Expiation or penalty, specifically the freeing of a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor required after Zahaar.

ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions and expiations for Zahaar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the origin of the 'Zahaar' vow, linking the specific incident of a woman's complaint to the revelation of Surah Al-Mujadila (58:1-4) and establishing the legal framework for this form of marital separation. It highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) role in interpreting divine revelation to resolve domestic disputes, while Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) further refines the jurisprudence by specifying that Zahaar requires a state of purity and absence of sexual intercourse, distinguishing it from general oaths. The narrative underscores the transition from the pre-Islamic practice of treating wives as mothers to a structured legal mechanism with specific expiations (kaffarah) to restore marital rights.
